citations.text:
[1] Here, mass spectrometry-calibrated intracellular flow cytometry of human hematopoiesis reveals MIIB
to be a major isoform that is strongly polarized in hematopoietic stem cells and progenitors (HSC/Ps) and
thereby downregulated in differentiated cells via asymmetric division.
[2] MIIA is constitutive and activated by dephosphorylation during cytokine-triggered differentiation of
cells grown on stiff, endosteum-like matrix, but not soft, marrow-like matrix.
[3] In vivo, MIIB is required for generation of blood, while MIIA is required for sustained HSC/P
engraftment.
[4] Reversible inhibition of both isoforms in culture with blebbistatin enriches for long-term hematopoietic
multilineage reconstituting cells by 5-fold or more as assessed in vivo.
[5] Megakaryocytes also become more polyploid, producing 4-fold more platelets.
